issues.description: The problem statement's UML and description specify Stock.take(String) should return an int (e.g., -1 on failure), but the template's Stock.take is declared to return boolean. The reference solution implements take(String) returning int. This mismatch in return type will cause compilation errors or confusion when students implement SealSaloon logic that expects an int result from stock.take.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Stock.take(String) method signature and implementation to return int (returning -1 on failure and the new quantity on success) to match the UML/problem statement and the reference solution. Alternatively, if the intent was boolean, update the problem statement and reference solution to use boolean consistently; prefer updating the template to int to match the specification and solution.

issues.description: The Stock.take method is represented differently across artifacts: the problem statement UML and the solution implement take(String) returning an int (using -1 to indicate failure), while the template implements take(String) returning a boolean. This mismatch in the method signature/return semantics for the same conceptual operation (removing/taking an ingredient from stock) creates confusion for students when mapping the problem requirements to the provided starter code and expected solution behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's Stock.take method signature and semantics match the problem statement and solution: change the template method to 'public int take(String ingredient)' and return -1 on failure (no ingredient or zero quantity), otherwise return the remaining quantity after decrement. This preserves the conceptual mapping and allows code that expects an int/-1 contract to work with the template.
